The journey begins with delicate white coffee blossoms. Flowering gives way to fruit, shaped by the growing season and the care of the farm team.
Green cherries develop along the branch. Fruit on the same tree can mature at different rates, so careful observation guides the harvest.
Unripe green coffee cherries on a branch
Ripe cherries are selected by hand while younger fruit remains on the tree for another round. Availability follows crop conditions.
A basket of handpicked coffee cherries at Nechekattu Farm
The harvest is sorted and prepared for its chosen method. Natural coffee dries in the whole cherry; pulped coffee has the outer skin removed.
Raised beds allow airflow beneath the coffee. Regular turning and monitoring help the team follow the drying progress of each lot.
Coffee cherries drying on raised beds at Nechekattu Farm
After drying and preparation, green coffee carries the work of the farm towards roasting and the cup. Discover the process on a seasonal farm visit.
